description: The LinkedIn analytics login-wall protocol written into reference/linkedin-analytics.md (by Rigby, from Harper's recommendation, approved in the Rock 4 wiring run) specifies STOP at any login wall and surface to David for manual re-login. David corrected: the protocol should instead use the op skill / 1Password CLI to auto-fill the LinkedIn username and password and continue autonomously. Do not block and wait for him.
correction: On a LinkedIn login wall, the path retrieves LinkedIn credentials from 1Password via the op CLI (installed, v2.34.1; op:// URI convention per projects/1password-integration.md), fills them via Playwright, handles 2FA from the vault's TOTP field if present, and continues. Blocking on David for a re-login the vault can handle is wasted executive attention. Never-fabricate still applies: if auth genuinely fails after autofill (wrong password, unanswerable 2FA, lockout), surface the failure — but never invent metrics and never block for a step that can be automated.
systemic_fix: Proposed: audit other IES protocols for the same stop-and-wait assumption where 1Password-retrievable credentials exist (Dynamics login, card portals already do autofill; LinkedIn was inconsistent with the established pattern). Default protocol: autofill via op, continue; block only on genuine unautomatable failure.
